artifacts.summary: Reproduces the reported false green: rules out scope_key normalization (a) and a fail-open missing-scope_key branch (b) by code reading; empirically REFUTES the literal cross-tree decide_sharing()-replay hypothesis (d) because compute_fingerprint()'s hash embeds each file's own path, which differs per worktree; but CONFIRMS a related, reproducible defect in the same dispatch-worktree.sh cp -al hardlink clone of .lake/: cross-tree flock lock serialization, and cross-tree build-guard.result/log clobbering exploitable as a real false green via the `result` subcommand's unguarded (no --expect-pid) read path. Recommends excluding build-guard.* from the .lake/ clone (not a tree-identity record field alone) since it also fixes the lock-contention defect, and names three regression tests to add under scripts/tests/.

memory_candidates.content: lake-build-guard.sh's compute_fingerprint() hashes a pre-image that embeds each source file's own absolute path (stat -c '%n %s %y', and sha256sum's own '<hash>  <filename>' output format does the same even in hash mode). This incidentally makes cross-tree fingerprint collisions impossible whenever two trees live at different absolute paths (e.g. main repo vs a dispatch-worktree.sh worktree under .orchestrate-worktrees/), which protects decide_sharing()'s replay branch from cross-tree false-sharing even though nothing in the design deliberately encodes tree identity. Don't rely on this staying true if compute_fingerprint() is ever changed to a pure content hash with no filename in the stream.

dispatch-worktree.sh's cp -al hardlink clone of .lake/ (and .claude/) shares the SAME INODE for any ephemeral runtime state file the cloned directory contains across the main tree and every worktree cloned from it. For lake-build-guard.sh this caused two confirmed, reproducible defects: (1) build-guard.lock being shared serializes a worktree's build against the main tree's build (defeats the 'mode 2' build-contention isolation dispatch-worktree.sh exists to provide), and (2) build-guard.result/.log/.stdout/.stderr being shared means a real build finishing in ANY cloned tree silently truncate-overwrites every other tree's own last verdict/log via finalize_record()'s '>' redirect -- exploitable as a false green through the `result` subcommand's unguarded (no --expect-pid) read path, though `build` mode's own exit code stays accurate since it never reads the record for its own return value. General lesson for any future hardlink-cloned directory: exclude ephemeral runtime/lock/result state files from the clone, only share build-output caches.

git rev-parse --git-common-dir is IDENTICAL across every worktree of one repository (it resolves to the shared main .git directory), so it cannot serve as a per-worktree tree-identity tag. git rev-parse --show-toplevel DOES differ per worktree (each worktree has its own checkout root) and is the correct source for a tree-identity field. Confirmed empirically with a throwaway git worktree pair.
